name: Dundee cake
origin: A traditional Scottish rich fruit cake from Dundee, associated with the Keiller marmalade-making family; distinguished from other British fruit cakes by its topping of concentric rings of whole blanched almonds.

ingredients.note: currants, sultanas, raisins and mixed peel together; dried fruit's own residual moisture (typically 15-20%) is not credited toward hydration here, a conservative simplification (see catalog.ts module notes)
a spoonful of marmalade stirred into the batter, a Dundee-specific touch tying the cake to the Keiller family's marmalade business

process.name: cream butter and sugar
process.description: beat butter and sugar until light

process.name: fold in flour and fruit
process.description: fold in flour, leavening and salt, then the dried fruit

process.name: arrange almonds and bake
process.description: arrange whole blanched almonds in rings on top, then bake low and slow

notes: Dried fruit at 3.5x flour mass is representative of published British rich fruit cake formulas (e.g. traditional Dundee cake recipes documented across British home-baking references); a long, low bake (rather than a hot, fast one) is real practice for a dense, fruit-heavy batter that would over-brown on the outside well before the crumb finished setting at a normal cake temperature.
